method: Commune zonal statistics over MODIS MCD64A1 burned area (binary burned mask x pixel area, summed) and FIRMS active-fire detections (per-pixel detection-day count, summed). Composite exposure index = weighted, sqrt-normalised burned fraction + detection density + recurrence (max commune = 100 per component).

sources.official: CONAF / itrend forest-fire statistics by commune (optional, local data/raw/ CSV; merged when present)

columns_description.fire_burned_area_km2_total: Cumulative burned area over the period (km^2)
columns_description.fire_burned_pct_mean_annual: Mean annual burned area as % of commune area
columns_description.fire_worst_year: Calendar year with the highest burned area for this commune
columns_description.fire_trend_km2_per_decade: Linear trend in annual burned area (km^2/decade, OLS slope x 10). Positive = increasing fire, negative = decreasing. Interpret cautiously: only 10 data points with high inter-annual variability.
columns_description.fire_detections_total: Total FIRMS detection-days over the period
columns_description.fire_detections_max_year: FIRMS detection-days in the worst year
columns_description.fire_brightness_max_k: Max FIRMS T21 brightness temperature (K). 0 = no fire detection in the entire period (not 0 Kelvin — used as sentinel).

brain_health_relevance.wildfire_smoke: Acute PM2.5/PM10 spikes -> neuroinflammation, cognitive decline
brain_health_relevance.recurrent_exposure: Chronic stress, displacement, loss of green space

limitations: MCD64A1 at 500 m underestimates small/urban fires; FIRMS complements it for interface fires. Dense urban communes are near-zero by design.
